I've found a gnarly instance diamond with docs#Ideal.Fiber. Any ideas on what to do about it?

import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.ResidueField.Fiber

/-
Tactic `rfl` failed: The left-hand side
  Localization.AtPrime.instAlgebraOfLiesOver p q
is not definitionally equal to the right-hand side
  OreLocalization.instAlgebra
-/
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
example {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [q.IsPrime] :
    (Localization.AtPrime.instAlgebraOfLiesOver p q) = OreLocalization.instAlgebra := by
  rfl
@Andrew Yang

Thankfully this is at least true mathematically, due to the universal property of localization:

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
example {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [q.IsPrime] :
    (Localization.AtPrime.instAlgebraOfLiesOver p q) = OreLocalization.instAlgebra := by
  apply Algebra.algebra_ext
  rw [← DFunLike.ext_iff]
  apply Localization.localRingHom_unique _
  · exact Ideal.LiesOver.over
  · intro x
    rfl
Localization.AtPrime.instAlgebraOfLiesOver p q is defined using RingHom.toAlgebra, that is usually a bad idea.
Trying to see if I can do better.

Writing down the thing with normal notation: we have an RRR-algebra SSS, a prime ideal p\mathfrak{p}p of RRR and a prime ideal q\mathfrak{q}q of T:=κ(p)⊗RST :=\kappa(\mathfrak{p}) \otimes_R ST:=κ(p)⊗R​S, where κ(p)=Rp/pRp\kappa(\mathfrak{p}) = R_{\mathfrak{p}}/\mathfrak{p}R_{\mathfrak{p}}κ(p)=Rp​/pRp​. Now, TqT_{\mathfrak{q}}Tq​ is a RpR_{\mathfrak{p}}Rp​-algebra in two ways: first of all via docs#Localization.AtPrime.instAlgebraOfLiesOver, since q\mathfrak{q}q lies over p\mathfrak{p}p and secondly via docs#OreLocalization.instAlgebra since it is the localization of TTT and TTT is already a RpR_{\mathfrak{p}}Rp​-algebra.

The problem is that docs#Localization.AtPrime.instAlgebraOfLiesOver, that is the usual algebra structure localizing at a prime below and a prime above, of course cannot assume that the big ring is already an algebra over the localization.

@Thomas Browning what happens if in the file you are considering you just deactivate the instance Localization.AtPrime.instAlgebraOfLiesOver? This is a suboptimal solution, but mathematically I would not say that q\mathfrak{q}q is above p\mathfrak{p}p (technically it is, but this is not the usual picture we have in mind).

Unfortunately it seems to break the statement that I'm trying to prove

Well, maybe not. From the ApA_pAp​-algebra structure you don't get the AAA-algebra structure automatically, and if you have both you cannot hope to have defeq
So in you case you can maybe just have the (stronger) instance saying that the fiber is an algebra over the localization of S.

A very similar situation that frequently appears in this context is with docs#IsLocalRing.ResidueField.instAlgebra and docs#IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebra.
These two are examples of the [Foo X Y] -> [Foo (F X) (F Y)] pattern that almost always causes a diamond in the Y = F X case.
Unfortunately, except for not making these instances available by default, I don't think there is much we can do about them?
Well, unfortunately I can't see a way around this diamond for my work in #37130, so I've opened a PR: #38452

I think docs#IsLocalRing.ResidueField.instAlgebra is a dangerous instance to have, and I'm surprised it made it into Mathlib.

We experimented in the FLT repo with [Algebra K L] -> [Algebra (AdeleRing K) (AdeleRing L)] and variants (finite adele ring, infinite adele ring) and it caused real problems -- lots of slowdowns. Now our approach is [Algebra K L] [Algebra (AdeleRing K) (AdeleRing L)] [add compatibilities here] and this seems to work much better in practice. So I would propose nuking IsLocalRing.ResidueField.instAlgebra and replacing it with hypotheses. Does this solve the problem?
